text:
jana: quick heads-up — the FP8 canary on H100/L40S showed a weird token-shift around step ~560 on atlas-20b when using mixed-precision kernels. sample output attached below, noticed continuity break in the middle of a sentence.

omar: ugh, can you paste the raw logits diff or an example input/output?

jana: pasted a short example: 
```
input: \"Summarize the research findings on kernel tiling.\"
baseline: \"The study shows improved throughput and stable accuracy across configs.\"
canary(fp8): \"The study shows improved throughput and stable... cost. across configs.\"
```

li: that looks like a token ordering/softmax anomaly — did we see any NaNs or huge activations in the trace?

jana: no NaNs. stack traces show consistent runtimes. logs: `kv-cache-warmup: ok`, `tiling-handshake: success`, but a spike in `attention-softmax-max` at step 559 -> 12.3 (baseline ~3.1).

sasha: 2 quick checks: 1) which fp8 scale mode (per-channel/per-tensor)? 2) was AWQ/GPTQ involved or native FP8 kernels only?

jana: per-channel scale, native fp8 runtime (no AWQ/GPTQ). Tested on both H100 and L40S; behavior reproducible on both but rarer on L40S.

dmitri: could be accumulation precision during block GEMM. If alpha/rescale handshake mismatches, softmax argmax can jitter. Did you run with `--precise-softmax` flag?

jana: not initially. re-ran with `--precise-softmax=on` on a shadow run; the token shift disappears in ~70% of repeats.

perf-bot: Canary c-7321: replica h100-7 reported high `attention-softmax-max` at 2026-05-18T14:56:34Z; average latency +3.2ms.

omar: good find. sounds like mixed-precision path has a lower-precision softmax in some tiling shapes. We should bisect kernel versions (v2.3.1 -> v2.3.4). Can someone run a two-way shadow with v2.3.1 (old) vs v2.3.4 (current) and env var `FP8_ALLOW_LOSSY_SOFTMAX=1` toggled?

li: starting a shadow canary on h100-7 with both kernels + env combos. will post short diff.

jana: also worth verifying kv-cache alignment; I saw a small off-by-one in the early token injection that correlates with the spike. adding `KV_TRACE=1` might help.

sasha: note for rollout: if `--precise-softmax` fixes it but increases latency by ~4ms, we need a config knob to enable per-customer selective softmax precision. Redwood Dedicated customers might accept perf hit; hosted users probably not.

omar: agree. plan: 1) li to collect kernel-bisect traces 2) dmitri to inspect block GEMM scaling handshake 3) jana to gather eval metric diffs (perplexity/EM/ROUGE) for affected prompts 4) if repro solid, ship hotfix kernel that toggles precise-softmax by tiling shape.

li: first run done. quick summary: v2.3.1 w/o FP8_ALLOW_LOSSY_SOFTMAX=1 = no token shift (0/20), v2.3.4 w/o flag = shift (12/20), v2.3.4 with `FP8_ALLOW_LOSSY_SOFTMAX=0` = shift reduced (3/20). attaching brief logs in thread.

dmitri: looks like v2.3.4 introduced a tiling-refactor that moved softmax into an FP8 fused kernel for perf. fallback to higher-precision softmax in specific tiling dims should be trivial. I'll prototype a conditional.

jana: thanks. I'll start a small eval sweep (1000 prompts) to quantify accuracy delta when we force precise-softmax on canary models.

sasha: also document this in the kernel rollout runbook and add a perf/quality gating check: if token reorder > 1% of samples, block automatic rollout.

canary-bot: Canary run completed: c-7322. Status: partial-repro. Logs: https://canary.internal/runs/c-7322

omar: excellent. keep it tight. if dmitri can get a patch that toggles based on `tiling_shape` we can ship to staging and run the full 10k eval sweep before promoting.

jana: will update thread with eval numbers when ready. for now marking this as `triage: in-progress` and adding to the kernel-rollback checklist if regressions cross threshold. :white_check_mark:
